name: Autarchism
summary: Autarchism is Robert LeFevre's name for total self-rule: each person governs himself and no one else, never initiating force against another person or property. It combines Stoic self-control, Epicurean self-interest and Austrian free-market economics, holds private property as a total principle, and treats the political state as an agency of molestation to be abandoned, not violently overthrown. LeFevre separated it from anarchism, which he called a branch of socialism, and Holmes records that it opposed physical force even in self-defence.
scope: The doctrine LeFevre called autarchy or autarchism, as set out in his Rampart Journal essays 'Autarchy Versus Anarchy' (1965) and 'Autarchy' (1966), and as Holmes (a scholarly review of the American libertarian movement) describes it as LeFevre's main teaching tenet. It excludes economic autarky (self-sufficient states), the anarchist socialist tradition LeFevre contrasts it with, and the wider libertarian movement.

sources.author: Robert LeFevre
sources.usedFor: Property as a total concept, support for profit, rent and interest, rejection of economic intervention and of socialist anarchism.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: LeFevre holds that Austrian economics shows the greatest good for the greatest number emerges in a free market and calls protection itself a free-market service (Autarchy, para 20, 71).

property-fundamental.rationale: He believes in property as a total concept and says a man may acquire all he can and use or abuse it as he pleases (Versus, paras 17, 84).

state-harmful.rationale: He calls political structures monsters of human contrivance capable of predation against all, and holds that the political state is the main source of molestation (Autarchy, paras 37, 57, 74).

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The autarchist will not coerce others even for their own good, and no individual or group may properly force any other (Autarchy, paras 30, 75).

political-violence-never.rationale: He says open rebellion strengthens authority and that autarchy is a bloodless individual revolution; Holmes reports his opposition to physical force even in self-defence (Autarchy, paras 66, 70; Holmes p. 91).

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Holmes reports that LeFevre's tenet autarchism combined self-ownership with consistent opposition to physical force, even for self-defence (p. 91).

self-ownership.rationale: Holmes names radical individualist self-ownership as the core of autarchism, and LeFevre defines it as the absolute sovereignty of the individual over himself and all that belongs to him (Versus, para 32).

self-interest-moral.rationale: LeFevre says the Epicureans rightly saw man as a profit-seeking creature and that pleasure, profit and gain are not forbidden, and he condemns enforced altruism (Autarchy, paras 6, 17, 75).

private-courts-defense.rationale: He says protection is a free-market service that people may buy and pool, though he stresses it is preventive, not retributive (Autarchy, paras 33, 71).

profit-exploitation.rationale: He supports profits, rents and interest without equivocation and rejects the view that they are usury (Versus, paras 40, 84).

land-use-tenure.rationale: He rejects Proudhon's possession-only tenure and Henry George's abolition of private land ownership, holding that an owner may own any kind or amount of property (Versus, paras 55, 60, 87).

taxation-theft.rationale: He treats taxation as violence that takes from an owner what is rightfully his and as trespass against taxpayers (Versus, para 87; Autarchy, paras 44, 55).

state-class-instrument.rationale: He describes political structures as a class culture in which some men have authority over and exploit others by force (Autarchy, para 7).

consent-of-governed.rationale: His principle is that no individual or group may force another against his will and all unions are by individual decision (Autarchy, paras 30, 34), which goes further than consent of the governed.

democracy-best.rationale: He calls majority rule a distortion of self-rule and says democrats like aristocrats coerce, so principles of autarchy vanish (Autarchy, paras 23, 31).

night-watchman-state.rationale: He holds political and military organizations are in themselves agencies of molestation and denies that constitutions limit them, so no limited government is endorsed (Autarchy, paras 37, 39, 43).

empower-police-military.rationale: He describes police and military as legalized armed bands financed by trespass on taxpayers (Autarchy, paras 44, 54).

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He treats military organizations as agencies of molestation and Holmes reports pacifism even in self-defence (Autarchy, paras 37, 44; Holmes p. 91).

conscription.rationale: Forcing persons into service is coercion he rejects, and he calls modern warfare mass sacrifice for the general good (Autarchy, paras 9, 30).

strong-leader.rationale: He says government by strong men creates pressure for another government by still stronger men (Autarchy, para 66).

one-party-rule.rationale: He denies anyone the authority to rule others, so a party leading the state contradicts his position (Autarchy, paras 22, 30).

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: He treats the divinely sanctioned ruler as part of the political mystique and rejects rule of one person over others (Autarchy, paras 24, 40).

total-state.rationale: He attacks the collective mystique, enforced altruism and the idea that the social whole outranks the individual (Autarchy, paras 6, 9, 18).

central-planning.rationale: He rejects the central planner and extra-market controls at any point of market participation (Versus, paras 34, 88).

public-ownership.rationale: Ownership by a coercive public body is political intervention he rejects, and he defends private ownership as a total concept (Versus, paras 37, 84).

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: He forbids compelling a seller or buyer to change the price of a product or service, and a legal wage floor does so (Autarchy, para 32).

universal-healthcare.rationale: A state-provided service paid by compulsory taxation is political coercion in his terms; services are sought by voluntary pooling (Autarchy, paras 33, 55).

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: He calls taxation violence against owners and defends holding any amount of property (Versus, para 87).

regulate-corporations.rationale: He opposes any regulatory or confiscatory force on owners of property regardless of kind or amount (Versus, para 13).

cut-welfare.rationale: He calls compulsory transfers enforced altruism at the common expense and says no one should be forced into cooperative endeavours for the common good (Autarchy, paras 6, 33); he does not state the dependency claim.

basic-income.rationale: A state income paid from compulsory taxation is enforced altruism in his terms (Autarchy, para 6).

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: He opposes political impositions on the free market at any point of market participation (Versus, para 88).

state-directs-investment.rationale: State direction of the economy is economic intervention he rejects at every point (Versus, paras 38, 88).

tax-inheritance.rationale: He defends the right of owners to hold any amount of property and condemns taxation as violence (Versus, para 87).

land-value-tax.rationale: He criticises Henry George's single tax, with all land rents to a central authority, as an intervention against private land ownership (Versus, paras 55, 58).

abolish-money-wages.rationale: He rejects the anarchist and syndicalist programme of eliminating profits and wage relations and upholds free economic contracts (Versus, paras 39, 73, 86).

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognized bodies setting wages and prices together are political controls on market exchange he rejects (Autarchy, para 32; Versus, para 88).

workers-councils.rationale: He rejects political power over others as such, and he opposes placing management control in workers' hands by democratic processes imposed on owners (Versus, para 14).

property-serves-common-good.rationale: He calls the common good a mystical illusion and holds a man may use or abuse his property as he pleases (Autarchy, para 11; Versus, para 17).

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: He supports profits, rents and interest without equivocation as returns to ownership (Versus, para 84).

distribution-by-process.rationale: He holds that a man must be free to acquire honestly all the property he can, a view based on how property was acquired (Versus, para 17).

resources-common-ownership.rationale: He rejects Henry George's abolition of private ownership of land and holds an individual may own any kind or amount of property (Versus, paras 55, 87).

economic-freedom.rationale: He says one who believes in freedom must believe in economic freedom, full latitude of choice in all economic areas (Versus, para 87).

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: He says autarchy preserves the right of the individual to say no, in contrast with the collectivist view that forbids a no (Autarchy, para 34).

no-compulsory-union.rationale: No one can be forced into any organization or cooperative endeavour; a union exists only if each party decides individually to join (Autarchy, paras 30, 33).

minority-veto.rationale: He says all parties to a union must decide individually, and that no individual or group may properly force any other to do anything against his will (Autarchy, para 30).

individual-rights-only.rationale: He calls the social whole a pleasant fiction and says the building material of any social unit is the individual (Autarchy, para 18).

positive-liberty.rationale: He defines freedom as self-rule free from impositions by any agency of force, with no mention of material means (Versus, paras 87, 89).

death-penalty.rationale: He treats state killing as part of the legalized murders of governments, and denies the state's authority to punish (Autarchy, paras 46, 54).

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Holmes reports his opposition to physical force even in self-defence, which rules out killing suspects without trial (Holmes p. 91).

civilians-legitimate-targets.rationale: Holmes reports his consistent opposition to physical force even in self-defence, and he decries war as mass sacrifice (Holmes p. 91; Autarchy, para 9).

war-builds-character.rationale: He says modern warfare is mass sacrifice and big governments lead to big wars (Autarchy, paras 9, 46).

military-superiority.rationale: He rejects maintaining armed political organizations and criticises the state's military expeditions (Autarchy, paras 37, 39).

territorial-expansion.rationale: He condemns empire as predation and the state's economic and military expeditions abroad (Autarchy, paras 39, 47).

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: He criticises the state's intervention in the affairs of other nations and holds force begets force (Autarchy, paras 39, 66).

force-without-un.rationale: He opposes state military expeditions without distinction between authorisations (Autarchy, para 39).

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Arming and funding violent insurgents is initiating force through the state, which he rejects (Autarchy, paras 39, 66).

non-intervention.rationale: He criticises the government for intervening in the affairs of other nationals around the world (Autarchy, para 39).

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: He treats war as mass sacrifice for the general good and Holmes reports his pacifism (Autarchy, para 9; Holmes p. 91).

abolish-income-tax.rationale: He calls taxation violence taking from an owner what is rightfully his (Versus, para 87).

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: His objection to taxation as violence implies cutting these taxes too (Versus, para 87); he does not discuss consumption taxes by name.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Taxation on any exchange is violence against owners in his terms (Versus, para 87).

pollution-taxes.rationale: He rejects taxation and extra-market restraints at any point of market participation (Versus, paras 87, 88).

targeted-social-spending.rationale: State social spending is enforced altruism at the common expense (Autarchy, para 6).

negative-income-tax.rationale: A state cash transfer financed by compulsory taxation is enforced altruism in his terms (Autarchy, para 6).

free-public-college.rationale: Tax-funded public provision is enforced altruism at the common expense (Autarchy, para 6).

free-basic-services-for-all.rationale: Tax-funded public provision is enforced altruism at the common expense (Autarchy, para 6).

job-guarantee.rationale: The state as employer financed by taxation is political coercion, and he opposes extra-market controls (Versus, para 88).

price-controls-essentials.rationale: He forbids compelling a seller to change the price: the seller is free to sell at any price desirable to him (Autarchy, para 32).

price-controls-fight-inflation.rationale: He forbids compelling a seller to change the price (Autarchy, para 32).

rent-control.rationale: He supports rents without equivocation and forbids compelling a seller to change the price (Versus, para 84; Autarchy, para 32).

maximum-personal-income.rationale: He says economic freedom is the right to own any kind or any amount of property (Versus, para 87).

legal-duty-to-work.rationale: Compelling work by law is coercion he rejects (Autarchy, para 30).

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: He supports rents without equivocation and defends voluntary unions in any property matter (Versus, paras 84, 87).

land-redistribution.rationale: Taking property by force is what he opposes, and he holds that owners may keep any kind or amount (Versus, paras 13, 87).

all-land-state-owned.rationale: He rejects Henry George's making land government property and defends private ownership of land (Versus, paras 55, 58).

municipal-property.rationale: He defends private ownership as a total concept and rejects ownership of productive property by political bodies (Versus, para 84).

municipal-businesses-mixed-economy.rationale: Governments running businesses financed by taxation is political intervention in the economy he rejects (Versus, paras 38, 88).

local-essentials-public.rationale: Public ownership of services is political intervention he rejects (Versus, para 88).

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: He attributes the labor theory of value to anarchists and Godwin's successors and follows Austrian economics against it (Versus, para 39; Autarchy, para 20).

class-collaboration.rationale: He describes economic cooperation as voluntary and mutually advantageous rather than a class struggle (Autarchy, para 8).

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He says communism leads to the abolition of human freedom and that a powerful totalitarian state would not wither away (Versus, paras 61, 63).

vanguard-party.rationale: A ruling party exercising authority over others contradicts his principle that each rules only himself (Autarchy, para 22).

smash-state-machine.rationale: He says governments must not be abolished but abandoned, and that rebellion strengthens authority (Autarchy, paras 66, 67).

means-match-ends.rationale: He argues that force begets force and that a society of self-rule comes through individual self-control, bloodlessly (Autarchy, paras 66, 70).

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: He argues open rebellion justifies stronger authority and rejects violent change (Autarchy, paras 66, 70).

property-sabotage-justified.rationale: He rejects any force against property and holds that property is a total concept (Versus, paras 84, 87).

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: He urges abandoning reliance on government rather than seeking to impose one's will through politics (Autarchy, paras 66, 69, 75).

separate-church-state.rationale: He holds that a man must be free to worship as he pleases or not at all, and that state force has no place in it (Versus, para 17).

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Enforcing religious law on others is coercion, and he says no one may force another against his will (Autarchy, para 30).

punish-blasphemy.rationale: He says a man must be free to worship as he pleases or not at all, and that force on a peaceful person is destructive (Versus, para 17).

apostasy-punishable.rationale: He says a man must be free to worship as he pleases or not at all (Versus, para 17).

restrict-conversion.rationale: Legal limits on peaceful religious choice are force on peaceful persons (Versus, para 17).

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: He holds that imposing force on a person peacefully pursuing his own objectives is destructive (Versus, para 17).

legalize-drugs.rationale: Prohibiting a peaceful person's conduct is force he rejects (Versus, para 17), and he asks that each be absolute ruler of himself (Versus, para 31).

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Prohibiting peaceful voluntary exchange is force he rejects (Versus, paras 17, 86).

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Legal restriction by state force on peaceful persons is what he opposes (Versus, para 17).

restrict-pornography.rationale: Legal restriction by state force on peaceful persons is what he opposes (Versus, para 17).

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: He opposes state force on peaceful persons and the idea that the common good justifies it (Autarchy, para 9).

internet-shutdowns.rationale: He opposes state force over peaceful activity in the name of order (Autarchy, para 9).

party-controls-media.rationale: Government control of information is the kind of coercion he rejects (Autarchy, paras 9, 30).

suppress-opposition.rationale: He says no one may be forced and condemns victimising dissenters for the general good (Autarchy, paras 9, 30).

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: He holds the state is itself a source of molestation and no group may force others (Autarchy, paras 30, 37).

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: He condemns legal murders, extortions and tortures by governments and says the state is the major source of trespass (Autarchy, paras 37, 46).

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: He opposes political controls on peaceful voluntary exchange (Versus, para 88).

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Political limits on who may own property contradict his view of ownership of any kind and amount (Versus, para 87).

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: He holds that an owner may hold any kind and amount of property and that voluntary unions are free (Versus, para 87).

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Law enforcing separation by state force on peaceful persons is what he opposes (Versus, para 17).

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: He defends the right to say no and rejects state compulsion in association (Autarchy, para 34).

limit-guns.rationale: He opposes state force against peaceful owners of property (Versus, para 17).

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: He treats the state's armed bands as the main source of molestation and holds protective tools may be bought by anyone (Autarchy, paras 33, 44).

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: He holds the political state has no claim on anyone's obedience and that individuals should deal with it by abandonment (Autarchy, paras 66, 68).

single-common-good.rationale: He calls the common good a mystical illusion and says individuals' interests differ beyond a few shared ones (Autarchy, paras 11, 12).

duties-before-rights.rationale: He calls enforced altruism the unvarying characteristic of political organization and rejects sacrifice of individuals to the general good (Autarchy, paras 6, 9).

person-over-state.rationale: He denies that any person may be sacrificed for the social whole, though he rejects the state itself (Autarchy, paras 9, 18).

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: He says those in government are as kind and cruel as anyone and that political organizations loot and kill for the good of the social whole (Autarchy, paras 47, 57).

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: State aid from taxation is enforced altruism at the common expense (Autarchy, para 6).

bound-labor.rationale: He rejects compelling anyone to labor for another (Autarchy, para 30).

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: He holds that each rules himself and no other (Autarchy, para 22).

sacred-ruler.rationale: He treats the divine sanction of rulers as part of the political mystique (Autarchy, paras 24, 40).

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He denies any ruler authority over others (Autarchy, paras 22, 30).

natural-rulers.rationale: Autarchy means each person rules himself, and no other (Autarchy, para 22).

leader-cult.rationale: He rejects mystique around political rulers and rule of men over men (Autarchy, paras 8, 40).

clerical-rule.rationale: He rejects any rule of men over others, including shamans (Autarchy, paras 9, 22).

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: He treats divine ordination of rulers as a political mystique and denies legitimate authority over others (Autarchy, paras 22, 40).

dynastic-succession.rationale: He rejects political rule by one person over others, hereditary or not (Autarchy, para 22).

elective-rulers.rationale: He says democratic selection of rulers who impose their wills is a distortion of self-rule (Autarchy, para 23).

parliament-supreme.rationale: He holds representative bodies merely channel unlimited political power (Autarchy, para 43).

mixed-constitution.rationale: He says dividing power among branches does not limit it (Autarchy, para 43).

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: He holds that constitutions binding lawmakers do not restrain the state (Autarchy, para 39).

ban-interest.rationale: He supports profits, rents and interest without equivocation (Versus, para 84).

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: He rejects the elimination of interest and profit and holds credit is a market matter (Versus, paras 39, 84).

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: He criticises Spooner's worry about large capital accumulations as a failure to grasp free-market economics (Versus, para 48).

no-business-privileges.rationale: He rebukes bankers and others who insist on dealing with the state (Versus, para 48).

no-bailouts.rationale: Rescuing firms from public funds takes from taxpayers by force, which he rejects (Versus, para 87).

free-trade.rationale: He argues the free market yields the greatest good for the greatest number and opposes extra-market restraints (Autarchy, para 20; Versus, para 88).

capital-controls.rationale: He rejects state restraints on market participation (Versus, para 88).

restrict-technology-exports-to-rivals.rationale: He rejects state restraints on market participation (Versus, para 88).

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: He rejects state-shaped economic blocs and defends voluntary exchange; he says autarky as a self-sustaining state is a corruption of his term (Autarchy, paras 22, 31).

ban-cartels.rationale: He holds that only coercion is to be excluded from the market and that voluntary organization of any size is allowed (Autarchy, para 35).

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: He holds that worship is a matter of individual choice and the state has no right to force belief (Versus, para 17).

state-supports-good-ways-of-life.rationale: He says the state may not impose a view of the good on individuals (Autarchy, paras 9, 30).

mandatory-environmental-reporting.rationale: He opposes regulatory force on owners (Versus, para 13).

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: A publicly funded system is paid by compulsory taxation, which he rejects (Versus, para 87).

public-service-media.rationale: Tax-funded media is paid by compulsory taxation, which he rejects (Versus, para 87).

student-debt-relief.rationale: Public relief paid by taxation takes from owners by force (Versus, para 87).

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Public top-ups paid by taxation are enforced altruism (Autarchy, para 6).

farm-price-support.rationale: Guaranteed prices and public purchase are extra-market controls he rejects (Versus, para 88).

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: State incentives paid by taxation are enforced altruism (Autarchy, para 6).

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding standards imposed by state agreements are extra-market restraints he rejects (Versus, para 88).

missingStatements.text: Protection against aggression should be bought voluntarily from providers people choose, not paid for by compulsory taxes.
missingStatements.rationale: LeFevre says protection is a free-market service to be purchased or pooled by those who wish it, and that no one can be forced into such an organization.

quotes.text: If one person wishes to buy protection, he has only to seek to purchase it. If others agree with him as to the amount and the kind of protection each is willing to buy, they have only to pool their energies or resources and thus procure it.
All that has to be added is the recognition that protection is neither more nor less than a free-market service.

notes: Sources are LeFevre's own essays plus one scholarly review (Holmes); no encyclopedia entry defining autarchism could be opened (libertarianism.org returned HTTP 429). Themes searched in the local library: government, economy, liberty, world and war, religion, property, means. LeFevre says nothing on culture, gender, ecology, technology, immigration, or most institutional design, so those answers are null. Answers on state provision and regulation rest on his rejection of taxation and coercion in economics, not on named programmes, so they are medium confidence. Holmes and Wikipedia report Rothbard's dispute with LeFevre over defensive force; the statement answers follow Holmes.
